metrics.test_coverage: Full coverage of testcase/selector_testcase.php and testcase/reader/selector_testcase.php

comments.note: testcase/reader/selector_testcase.php line 24 uses str_get_dom() which is an undocumented alias. The reader test file has ~15 commented-out test sections with no explanation. This dead/commented code adds confusion about the reader module's intended behavior vs what is actually tested.

testcase/selector_testcase.php mixes global variable $dom with str_get_html() reassignment in a single procedural script. The resulting non-isolated fixture state makes it hard to reason about which tests reset the DOM. The new PHPUnit structure resolves this by using proper setUp()/tearDown() lifecycle per test.

tests/Selectors/SelectorTest.php and ReaderSelectorTest.php share many repeated HTML fixture strings (e.g., the checkbox input, image tag, nested div HTML). A shared data provider or a protected helper could reduce duplication across the two classes.

The original reader test file expected different results than the main library for namespace and pseudo-tag selectors (count=0 vs count=1). This divergence is undocumented and suggests either a past feature divergence between the reader module and main library, or stale/incorrect legacy test expectations.

summary: Code review of tests/Selectors/SelectorTest.php and tests/Selectors/ReaderSelectorTest.php. Both files are comprehensive, well-organised, and document behavioral differences from the reader library explicitly. All acceptance criteria confirmed met by QA. No blocking issues. Two low-priority non-blocking observations recorded.

comments.note:
SelectorTest.php — the div+img fixture ('
\n...
') is duplicated across 7 test methods (testWildcardSelector, testTagSelector, testClassSelector, testIndexSelector, testIdSelector, testAttrSelector, testWildcardAttrSelector). A private helper method or class constant would reduce copy-paste maintenance risk. Non-blocking.

ReaderSelectorTest.php::testNestedTableClassSelector and testNestedSelectorWithLoop use local $dom = str_get_html(...) with manual $dom->clear() at the end. If any assertion fails before clear(), the DOM object leaks. This is the same recurring pattern noted in WP-003's ReaderElementTest.php. Root cause: str_get_html() needs non-default parameters that can't be pre-set in setUp(). Consider assigning to $this->dom after construction to leverage tearDown().
